q: How does the lcp-inspect daemon come up in dndcs?
a: pnpm dev is three scripts: inspect runs node ../lcp_inspect/bin/lcp-inspect.mjs serve unless curl already answers on http://localhost:4848/__lcp/repos, brave opens http://localhost:5173 in Brave only when no Brave Browser process is running, and vite itself. The curl guard is needed because serve() in lcp-inspect has no EADDRINUSE handler and a second daemon on 4848 throws.

q: Is there a block sidebar on a page being written?
a: Yes, since 2026-09-11. BlockSidebar in src/components/ui is MarBlockEditorSidebar: the slash commands under their group names, each item with its icon or mark, title and description; a press without travel adds the block at the end through the editor's addBlock export, a press that travels past four pixels hands it to startExternalDrag so it drops where the pointer lands. ResourceShell slides it in and out beside the editor through the Sidebar component inside page-write, a grid whose second column opens to three space-8, toggled by the blocks glyph in the writing acts.

q: How does the block editor match MarBlockEditor now?
a: In full since 2026-09-11. Two gutter IconBtns per block, more for the typed options menu and grip for dragging; the options are per kind as in blockOptions.ts, with width, wrap, leading and view on the options and justify and xl added. Bullet, number and todo nest with Tab and Shift+Tab through a depth written as two spaces per level. Props are value, editable, placeholder, commands, onsearch for @ and # resolved asynchronously, onchange, onpage returning the id, onfile, onasset, onpreview and headingNumbering; the component exports getMarkdown, getHTML, getBlocks and startExternalDrag. BLOCK_COMMANDS is the exported slash list.

q: What block kinds does the editor carry?
a: Twenty five since 2026-09-11: paragraph, heading, quote, code, bullet, number, divider, callout, image, task, table, toggle, poll, audio, bookmark, then mermaid, html, toc, columns, video, pdf, embed, meeting, map and page. Fenced blocks with an info string carry mermaid, html, embed, meeting, map and columns, [toc] is a directive line, video, pdf and page are link lines with a kind marker. Mermaid renders through the mermaid package imported dynamically in the reader only; html is stripped of script, iframe, on attributes and javascript addresses first.

q: What does pressing a row on a roll do?
a: It peeks: the resource opens in roll-peek, a sticky aside on the right at 30 percent with a minimum of three space-8, in the home page's side area design: a dnd-label divide with the mark, an Open and a Close IconBtn, the picture at 3 by 2, the title, the lede, the tags and the page through BlockReader. Pressing the same row again or Close puts it away; under 50rem the aside falls below the list. The Open action on the row or in the peek goes to the detail page.

q: How are resources grouped on a roll?
a: A group is a document on the same roll with group true and only a title; a member carries the group's id in group_id. getAll(owner, kind) leaves groups out and getAll(owner, kind, true) returns only them. On a campaign roll the DM presses Arrange in the head acts: New group makes one, headers gain rename and dissolve, and rows drag onto a group header or the ungrouped area, each drop written at once through putOne. Dissolving clears every member's group_id then deletes the group. Groups are shared with the campaign so every member reads them.

q: How does a resource list page draw its rows?
a: ResourceRoll draws a tree of Row elements from src/components/ui: group headers, a dnd-label band with a caret, count and run that folds with unfold, each holding its members, then the ungrouped rows. Row is a div with a press button and, when onopen is given, an Open IconBtn at the end; it draws the picture square at the start. The page snippet is row(one, under, peek): a press peeks, the Open action navigates. The head is the same dnd-band as the detail pages: the campaign or Your own as the eyebrow with the acts at the end, then the hero title and a mono count. Since 2026-09-11.

q: How does a resource list page draw its rows?
a: As Row in src/components/ui, one per resource, the way PlaceListPage set: title, description as the sub line, RESOURCES kind mark as the end mark, the tags as verdigris hash words and the type's own columns as spans. ResourceRoll lays rows out as list by default since 2026-09-10; the grid of cards is not a list page. ResourceCard stays for the campaign overview and the lore panel.

q: How are a resource's pictures shown?
a: The face at the head is a button: the main picture square at the head's height, or the Portrait at size fill with the traced frame drawn around it when one.frame is set. The gallery strip sits right under the face at its width on a raised band, folds away with the head, and both open GalleryDialog in src/components: a fixed full screen overlay above the bar with no dialog chrome, IconBtn controls laid over the picture for close, previous, next, zoom out, zoom in, fit and make this the main picture, a thumbnail strip, wheel zoom only with cmd or ctrl held, drag to pan when zoomed, and a click on the ground closes it.

q: How is the resource head laid out?
a: page-band-grid has two columns: page-side, the picture with the gallery strip as one line right under it at the picture's width, and page-band-main, which stacks the line of breadcrumb and action icons, the crown of title and lede, and the head of facts. The face is square at page-band-main's measured height through bind:clientHeight, or the traced Portrait when a frame is set. Under a 40rem container the grid is one column with the side ordered after the main, full width at 3 by 2.

q: How is the resource head laid out?
a: Two rows in page-head-band. page-band-line is one flex line: the breadcrumb eyebrow at the start and the action icons at the end. Under it page-band-grid has areas face over crown and head, columns auto and 1fr, so the title, lede and facts take the full width beside the picture; the face is square at the grid's measured height, or the traced Portrait when a frame is set, and a container query under 40rem stacks face, crown and head.

q: How are a resource's pictures shown?
a: The face at the head is a button: the main picture square at the head's height, or the Portrait at size fill with the traced frame drawn around it when one.frame is set. Every picture sits in page-gallery at the foot of the body, a horizontal scroll-snap strip. Both open GalleryDialog in src/components: a stage with previous and next, zoom by buttons, plus and minus keys, or wheel with cmd or ctrl held, drag to pan when zoomed, a thumbnail strip, and Make this the main picture which writes at once through keepMain while reading.

q: How is the resource head laid out?
a: A page-band-grid with areas face, crown, acts over face, head, head. The face is the main picture, square at the grid's measured height through bind:clientHeight and object-fit cover, clipped by the chosen Portrait frame through an objectBoundingBox clipPath when one.frame is set; a container query under 40rem stacks it full width at 3 by 2. Access carries the key glyph, the gear opens FrameDialog and writes the frame at once while reading, and the shelf of thumbnails only draws with more than one picture.

q: What is Picker and where is it used?
a: src/components/ui/Picker.svelte, a chip well with a typeahead dropdown. picked and options are Pick rows with id, mark, name and an optional word and tone; free names the mark a typed entry is minted with on Enter, comma or blur, and more plus onmore add a row at the foot of the dropdown. ResourceAccess uses two for who reads it and what they get, and ResourceShell uses one for tags over every tag on the roll.

q: How does a fold open and shut?
a: The unfold action in src/lib/unfold.ts, the MarAccordionItem method: the body is always drawn, max-height animates from the measured scrollHeight to zero and back, and once open it is let go to none so the content may grow. Fold, Tree, the resource head and its kids, and the campaign introduction all use it; nothing is drawn with an if block for a collapse.

q: Does a resource page say Saved, or carry a Remove button?
a: No, ruled out by the user 2026-09-10. Nothing is stated after a save, the danger Remove button and deleteOne are gone from ResourceShell, and the edit acts bar is the same bare icon row as the read acts so it never changes size.

q: How does a button show its tooltip?
a: The title attribute, drawn by app.css as a styled ::after on hover and focus-visible for .dnd-sigil, .dnd-iconbtn and .dnd-button, so every button primitive gets one for free. It sits above by default, below on the Shell bar, and to the left of the chat action column, so it is never clipped by an overflow hidden box.

q: What keeps a drawer open across navigation, and what draws it?
a: Every page mounts its own Shell, so drawer state cannot live in Shell. Since 2026-09-10 menuOpen and chatOpen sit in uiStore with toggleMenu and toggleChat, and Shell reads the derived stores. Both drawers are Sidebar in src/components/ui, the MarSidebar principle: an aside that translates in and out with an absolutely positioned inner laid out at the run width, so the content never scales down while the grid column collapses.

q: How does a resource page edit inline?
a: Since 2026-09-10 the title and lede hosts and every fact input sit unboxed in the read position: the title host carries dnd-heading dnd-heading-hero, the facts form is a dl.dnd-facts with a label in dt and the input in dd, styled by .dnd-facts input in app.css with only a hairline under it on focus. Add a picture is an IconBtn with the picture glyph in the read acts and saves at once through putOne; the Pictures part draws only when there are pictures, so the facts sit at the left edge.

q: How is a resource shared, and what does the access dialog carry?
a: Access holds share_campaigns, share_parties and share_users as id lists, no share enum and no single share_party since 2026-09-10. ResourceAccess is two tag pickers, built as one snippet in the dialog: Who reads it takes campaigns, parties and people from the user's own campaigns, parties and friends with an Add by email row at the foot of the dropdown, and What they get lists the owner's resources across every kind with the open one preselected. Save writes the three lists and readers, from getReaders with the picked campaigns' and parties' members, onto every picked resource through putOne.

q: How is a document written out as mail?
a: getDocumentEmailHtml in blocks.ts, a pure function needing no service. A whole html document laid out in tables with every style inline and no style element, because a mail client keeps no sheet. A block a mail client cannot mount degrades to its own content or to a link rather than to an empty tag: a poll becomes its tally, a recording becomes a link, a toggle becomes its own content unfolded. What the author wrote is escaped rather than becoming markup. test/blocks-mail.spec.ts pins all of it.

q: What block kinds does the editor carry?
a: Fifteen. The nine it began with, paragraph, heading, quote, code, bullet, number, divider, callout and image, then task, table, toggle, poll, audio and bookmark. A poll holds the question on its first line and a choice on each line after, and its votes as a uid to choice map in the fence, so a second press on the same choice takes the vote back. Audio records through MediaRecorder and stores through postFile, the one uploader the app keeps. Bookmark holds its address in the fence. A block id is made fresh on every parse, so a poll is identified by where it sits, never by id.

q: What happens when a written reference is pressed?
a: It resolves against what the rolls actually hold. A hash word opens that kind's roll with tag in the search, and ResourceRoll reads it and lights the chip, so the roll opens already narrowed. An at name is looked for on the roll being read first, then on every other roll in turn, and the address it opens belongs to whichever roll answered, so a character named on a quest opens the character page. A name nothing answers to says so rather than opening the wrong page. BlockReader has always emitted the reference; before this nothing listened.

q: What look can a block carry of its own?
a: Alignment and type size, set from the block menu under Set and Size. A block takes the page's look until it is given one of its own, which is what the own flag marks, and Take the page's look hands it back. Task, table and toggle are block kinds beside the original nine; a task carries done and strikes through, a toggle carries open and reads as a details, a table splits its rows on newlines and its cells on pipes with the first row as the head.

q: How does a block keep what markdown cannot say?
a: In a fence, following MarBlockEditor's grammar. The info string is the block name then its own options as json, the body is the block's text, and the fence opens and closes with one more backtick than the longest run inside it so blocks nest to any depth. A block that carries nothing of its own is still written as plain markdown, so a heading stays a heading. Anywhere that does not know the grammar it reads as a labelled code fence. test/blocks-grammar.spec.ts pins the round trip for table, toggle, task and a block carrying its own look.

q: What does the block editor do beyond typing?
a: The handle does two jobs, told apart by a four pixel threshold: a press that lifts where it landed opens the block menu, a press that travels drags the block to a new place, taking pointer capture at the threshold. Markdown is the clipboard format: pasting markdown becomes blocks through getBlocksFromMarkdown, copying a whole block or a multi block selection writes markdown out. A selection that crosses a block boundary is drawn by the editor rather than the browser, because each block is its own textarea and a native range stops at the host it started in; Backspace or Delete removes the selected blocks and leaves one empty paragraph, an arrow collapses it, and cmd or ctrl A grows from

q: What does a resource roll draw and how is it filtered?
a: ResourceRoll takes kind plus row, and optionally tools, order, keep and layout of grid or list. It draws a filter bar under the header: the type's own controls from tools, then a chip per tag found across the rows which filters by every picked tag, then Clear. order sorts and keep filters on the type's own fields. Places is the first list rather than a grid, ordered by name, tag, area or map and filtered by kind, drawn with Row. Row is the ui primitive for a full width page list line, as Card is the medallion and Tree is the sidebar. User, 2026-09-09.

q: What sidebar does a resource page carry?
a: The campaign navigator, MenuPanel, the same one every other page carries. The bespoke per kind Pages aside on the resource page is gone. MainMenu now folds every kind, Campaign details, Players, Characters, Places, Maps, Encounters then Quests, Sessions, Entries, Items, Weapons, Armor and Heroes, each a Tree, and it reads the address rather than route params: the routes are literal per kind so params.kind no longer exists, and the open fold and the highlighted row come from the path segments. User, 2026-09-09.

q: How is a resource edited, and what does the edit bar carry?
a: Inline on the page, never a route. The Edit action sets a local editing flag; there is no /edit address and the resource routes are the roll, the resource and create only. Edit is disabled, with the reason in its title, unless the signed in user is the resource's owner_id. While editing the header actions are replaced by a pill with a translucent blurred background carrying Back, Forward, Revert and Save. Back and Forward walk a snapshot history of the whole resource plus the tag line, Revert restores the snapshot taken when editing opened, and Save writes and closes editing. The bottom row keeps only Create and Cancel while fresh, and Remove otherwise. User, 2026-09-09.

q: What do the resource pages share?
a: Two scaffolds in src/components/campaign. ResourceShell takes kind plus a facts snippet and a form snippet and owns the address, the load, the crown, the pictures, the tags, the content editor, the page tree, save, delete and the Access dialog. ResourceRoll takes kind plus a row snippet and owns the search, the count, the Add button and the grid. The dl of facts uses the global dnd-facts class in app.css, because a snippet is authored in the page and scoped styles follow the page, so a shared look has to be global or it would be repeated ten times.

q: What are the resource pages called and where do they sit?
a: src/pages/resource/ holds twenty pages, one per kind per address: EntryPage and EntryListPage, NpcPage and NpcListPage for the characters kind, HeroPage, ItemPage, WeaponPage, ArmorPage, PlacePage, MapPage, SessionPage, QuestPage and each ListPage beside it. The NPC pages are named Npc after the npcs collection because CharacterPage is the character sheet; the screen still reads Characters. Each page owns its own facts, its own form fields and its own card stats, and is around forty lines. src/App.svelte maps kind to the two page loaders in RESOURCE_PAGES.

q: Is there one page per resource type, or two generic pages?
a: One page per type. Every resource kind has its own page component and lays out its own facts; what they have in common is extracted as components they share, never a single generic page branching on kind. This reverses the 2026-09-08 answer that there are two generic pages, RecordListPage and RecordPage, driven by a SHAPES table and never one page per type. User, 2026-09-09.

q: What must an effect guard in this app converge on?
a: The not-found path as well as the found one. An effect that picks a record out of a list must key its guard on a token that settles whether or not the record is there, such as recordId over all.length over held or void. Writing the marker to the record id and then clearing it when the record is absent oscillates forever and Svelte throws effect_update_depth_exceeded. This bites whenever a list can legitimately come back empty, which it now can, since every list read is a readers array-contains query.

q: How is the access dialog constructed?
a: ResourceAccess follows the nimployer dialog construction with the dndcs design. Gather locally then commit once: a single dropdown names the reach rather than toggle buttons, a second names the party when the reach is party, a row list holds the named people, and a footer carries Cancel and Save with Save disabled until something changed and the party is picked. Loading draws dnd-loading, an empty people list draws dnd-empty, and busy is a string naming what is running rather than a boolean, so one row can be busy alone. Nothing writes until Save, which recomputes readers and closes.

q: Where does the starter page for a new resource come from?
a: RESOURCES in src/lib/resources.ts carries an example per kind, markdown that getDocument parses into blocks, and ResourcePage's blank() seeds content with RESOURCES[kind].example so a create address opens on a skeleton instead of one empty paragraph. All ten kinds have one. BlockEditor reads value once at mount into its own blocks state and does not react to a later value change, so the seed has to be on the resource before the editor renders.

q: What draws a dense list in a sidebar?
a: Tree in src/components/ui. A nested ul of 26px rows: a caret when a row has kids, the title, and a dim mark at the end, with on and onopen as props. It replaces ResourceCard in the navigator and the hand rolled page-aside-row tree on ResourcePage, which were 74px medallion cards and unreadable once a campaign had more than a handful of anything. ResourceCard stays for a grid of resources on a list page, never for a drawer. User, 2026-09-09.

q: Is a party a thing of its own, or only a view of a campaign?
a: A party is its own entity, not a subset of a campaign's members. A party can be created on its own just to chat and use the character sheets together, with no campaign around it, and a campaign includes both a party and the campaign membership. This reverses the 2026-09-07 answer that a party exists only inside a campaign. User, 2026-09-09.

q: Who may read a resource, and does the DM override it?
a: The owner of a resource, the uid that created it, has full access to it. Sharing is the owner's choice and it binds the DM too: a resource the owner did not share with the DM is genuinely hidden from the DM, and the DM's own lists can therefore be incomplete. There is no DM sees all override. is_known is replaced by access: sharing is the only visibility and the Hidden badge and the reveal mechanic go with it. Targets are the campaign, a party, or named individual users. User, 2026-09-09.

q: What are the resource addresses in dndcs?
a: Six per kind, registered as literal routes generated over Object.keys(RESOURCES) in App.svelte. Campaign owned: /campaign/:id/<kind>, /campaign/:id/<kind>/:resourceId, /campaign/:id/<kind>/:resourceId/edit. User owned: /<kind>, /<kind>/:resourceId, /<kind>/:resourceId/edit. create sits in the resourceId slot, never a segment of its own, because the router sorts patterns by string length so /<kind>/:resourceId would swallow a literal /<kind>/create. A bare /:kind pattern is forbidden for the same sort reason: it outranks /user and /main and would swallow them.

q: Why must a route component never take a required prop in dndcs?
a: sly-svelte-location-router re-renders the previous route component with props null during the load window: Router.svelte keeps StableComp pointing at the old component while activeProps goes null, so any required prop is undefined for one frame and a derived like RESOURCES[kind] throws. Route props declared in the routes table are therefore unusable. A page reads its own address instead, $resolvedRoute.path split into steps, and guards the kind with isResourceKind so a stale render of the old page against a new path cannot crash.

q: Where does a resource that belongs to a user, not a campaign, live?
a: At users/{uid}/{kind}, mirroring the campaign subcollections at campaigns/{id}/{kind}. The readers and writers in src/lib/resources.ts take an owner rather than a campaignId, so the same generic pages serve both. The addresses are /campaign/:id/:kind/:resourceId for a campaign resource and /:kind/:resourceId for a user resource. Settled 2026-09-09.

q: Is maps a resource like the others, or a tab on the campaign page?
a: Maps is literally every other resource. It routes to /campaign/:id/maps through ResourceListPage and ResourcePage like characters, quests, places, items, weapons and armor. It must not sit in the TABS array in CampaignPage.svelte, which intercepts it at openRoll and flips a local tab instead of navigating. Party is intercepted the same way and is wrong for the same reason.

q: Why could no pin be placed on a map?
a: setPointerCapture ran on pointerdown, and a captured pointer retargets the following click to the capturing element, so the click landed on the viewport and the .dnd-map-catcher button's handler never fired. The capture now happens on the first pointermove past the drag threshold, so a click reaches the catcher and a drag still pans.

q: How does the map draw?
a: A canvas. MapCanvas paints the base layer and every area layer onto one canvas sized to the viewport times devicePixelRatio, with the pan and zoom applied by setTransform and imageSmoothingQuality high, so nothing is resampled by a CSS transform. Pins stay DOM buttons positioned in viewport space by screen(marker), which keeps them accessible and unblurred; a click places by the exact inverse of that projection.

q: Where is Card used?
a: Everywhere a thing is listed, and nothing else draws one. Resources go through ResourceCard; the party, the players, the maps and the encounters in the navigator, the hearth's lists, and the map's hover popup all draw a Card directly. A bespoke row or tally for a listed thing is the drift that made a quest look different on every page.

q: Does the navigator sidebar follow the address?
a: Yes. MainMenu derives the open fold from currentRoute params kind, mapping characters, places, maps to their own folds, heroes and party to Players, and everything else to Campaign details; tab=maps in the search opens Maps. The resource being read is marked with Card's on prop, which ResourceCard passes through, so the drawer shows where you are.

q: How does the top bar navigation handle overflow?
a: Stops in src/components/ui draws the stops inline and collapses to one IconBtn plus the current stop's name with a dropdown when they do not fit. It measures a hidden ghost row against its own width, so .dnd-shell-nav carries flex 20 1 0 and .dnd-shell-run flex 1 1 0: a content independent basis is what stops the collapse latching, because a nav sized by its content shrinks the moment it collapses and never expands again. CampaignPage and ResourceListPage both pass their stops to it.

q: What are the campaign sections called on screen?
a: Party for the character sheets at the table, Characters for the NPCs, Places, Quests, Sessions, Maps, Entries. Cast, Lore and The world are dead names and must not appear: the campaign overview headers, the navigator sidebar folds and the top bar all read from the same vocabulary. The npcs and locations Firestore collections keep their old names.

q: How is a resource drawn on a page?
a: One way everywhere: ResourceCard in src/components/campaign wraps Card and opens /campaign/:id/:kind/:resourceId. RESOURCES carries a mark per type, the one fact that tells that type apart, which is the badge; an unrevealed resource reads Hidden instead. The campaign overview, the navigator sidebar and the list page all draw it, so a quest looks the same wherever it appears. Every page reads through resources.ts getAll, never campaignService, so there is one shape; Resource carries created_at for the chronicle.

q: How is the address changed?
a: Only by navigate from sly-svelte-location-router. Never history.pushState or replaceState by hand: navigate short-circuits when the address already equals the target, so a hand rolled rewrite desyncs the router and makes the next navigate to that path do nothing. MainPage's replaceState to /main ran after navigate had pushed a campaign path and dragged the address back, so the campaign rendered under /main. The routes map redirect / to /main handles the root.

q: How does a map zoom?
a: Only with cmd or ctrl held, on MapCanvas onWheel, which returns before preventDefault when neither is down. A plain wheel scrolls the page as normal. The campaign page no longer carries a crown header, only the shell bar and the CampaignBar band.

q: What organizes a sidebar?
a: Fold in src/components/ui. A band with a caret, a title and a count over a body drawn only when open. MainMenu and the map sidebar both stack them so every drawer reads the same, and open plus ontoggle are props so a caller picks accordion or many open at once.

q: How does a page fill the content edge to edge?
a: Shell takes flush, which drops the hold's padding, gap, max-width and auto margin and turns the scroll into a flex column so the body takes the height left under the bars. CampaignPage sets it on the maps tab, so the map runs to all four edges under the shell bar and the CampaignBar band.

q: What opens the chat?
a: Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + C toggles the chat. Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + S toggles the left sidebar and only that; it no longer cycles into the chat. Both live in stepDrawers on svelte:window in Shell, and each does nothing when the page did not give that drawer. Corrected 2026-09-08.

q: What opens the chat?
a: Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + C toggles it directly, because the chat is on every page. Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + S still steps through whichever drawers the page gave, none to menu to chat to none. Both live in stepDrawers on svelte:window in Shell. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How is a resource page laid out?
a: A header band carries the breadcrumb, the title, the description, the pictures, the static fields and the tags; the content fills the rest of the page under it. Shell's .dnd-shell-hold has min-height 100% so a page child with flex 1 actually fills, which is what the content section uses. No resource ever renders as a list of open forms. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: What does the shell bar carry?
a: Four handles: the menu, About this table, search and chat. test/sigils.spec.ts pins the count, the glyph order and that every bar sigil passes nothing but title, size, active and onclick, so adding one to the bar means updating that contract in the same change. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: What shape does every resource share?
a: There is no shared record type and never was; that was a hallucination. src/lib/resources.ts declares each resource as its own named interface, Entry, Character, Hero, Item, Weapon, Armor, Place, Chart and Quest, each extending Resource, which only names the fields they all carry: title, description, tags, images, image, content, parent_id, is_known. Each type has its own explicit functions, getWeapons, postWeapon, putWeapon, deleteWeapon and the same per type, never a generic writer. Never the word Row in a name. Corrected 2026-09-08.

q: How is a record edited?
a: Inline on the page it is already on, never a separate screen. RecordPage holds a writing flag: reading shows the title, the lede, the facts, the tags, the gallery and BlockReader; writing swaps the same layout to inputs and BlockEditor with Save, Cancel and Remove. Creating is the same page at /new with the crown reading New, and only the create button differs. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How does a record hold sub pages?
a: parent_id on the record. getRoots, getChildren and getTrail in records.ts walk the tree. Slash page in BlockEditor fires onpage, which writes a child record carrying the parent id and leaves a [[title]] link in the block; RecordPage draws the children as tabs above the content and the whole tree in the left drawer with a New page button. Settled 2026-09-08, LegendKeeper is the reference.

q: What shape does every resource share?
a: Title, description, tags, images, the main image chosen out of those images, and content as a block document. src/lib/records.ts holds the one RecordRow, getRow reads any stored record of any age into it and getPayload writes it back, so a type only declares the static fields that make sense for it. The nine types are entries, characters, heroes, items, weapons, armour, places, maps and quests, each naming the campaign subcollection it lives in. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How does a record open?
a: Reading, then editing, never straight into a form. /campaign/:id/:kind/:recordId is the view: the facts, the pictures and the body through BlockReader, with Edit, Who sees this and Back. /campaign/:id/:kind/:recordId/edit and /campaign/:id/:kind/new are the form, which leaves the campaign navigation behind: no navigator drawer, and the crown reads the roll and whether it is new, editing or reading. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How does a campaign navigate?
a: One bar, CampaignBar, shared by CampaignPage and RecordListPage so navigation is continuous. A select names the section and the bar beside it shows only that section's sub navigation, never both levels flat. Sections are Overview, Story, People with Party and Characters, World with Maps and Places, and Library with Items and Entries. getSection maps a stop back to its section so a page opened from a link shows the right one. Settled 2026-09-08 after the flat bar was rejected several times.

q: Which button primitive does a control use?
a: Button carries a word. IconBtn is a glyph and nothing around it, no border and no background, and is the default for any glyph only control. FrameBtn is a glyph inside a Sigil frame and is the exception that has to earn its frame. Stat is the pressable plate that shows a figure. No primitive takes a size prop: a button is square and fills the height it is given, so the row decides how big it is. .claude/rules/buttons.md carries this. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How does a map layer cover an area?
a: MapLayer carries optional x, y, width and height as fractions of the map. A layer with no width is a whole map replacement and the highest banded one wins; a layer with a width is an area overlay drawn at those bounds on top of the base, so several can light at once and zooming in reveals more detail per region. MapCanvas splits them into whole and areas and the DM edits the bounds on the layer row. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How is access granted on a record?
a: Per item, never a list. CampaignAccess takes kind, id, name and a bindable isKnown and opens from a Who sees this button on RecordPage; it writes through putRecordRow and shows the table settings underneath only when the campaign record is handed in. The old dialog that listed every map, npc, place and quest at once is gone. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How do the record pages work?
a: Two generic pages driven by src/lib/records.ts, never one page per type. RecordListPage at /campaign/:id/:kind lists with an Add button at the top; RecordPage at /campaign/:id/:kind/:recordId is both create and edit, with recordId of 'new' meaning create. SHAPES declares the fields per kind and getRecordRows, postRecordRow, putRecordRow and deleteRecordRow dispatch to the right service method. Kinds are characters, items, places and entries. Every record carries a block document in body, a list of images, and image_url as the portrait picked by clicking a picture.

q: What are the campaign record types called?
a: Characters, Items and Places, plus quests and sessions. Cast is gone as a name. The Firestore collections keep their old names, npcs and locations, and items was added as a fifth; the catch-all match /{part}/{recordId} in firestore.rules already governs it so no rules change was needed. CampaignRecordKind is the display vocabulary, 'place' | 'character' | 'item' | 'quest' | 'session'. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: What is the block editor and where did it come from?
a: src/lib/blocks.ts plus BlockEditor.svelte and BlockReader.svelte in src/components/ui. The concepts were copied from MarBlockEditor in the components-nimtech repo and rebuilt here in Svelte with the Mar prefix dropped; the package is NOT a dependency and must never be imported. A document is { blocks: [{ id, kind, text, options }] } with kinds paragraph, heading, quote, code, bullet, number, divider, callout, image. getDocument reads either the stored JSON or older markdown, getDocumentMarkdown writes it back, and getReferences pulls the @ mentions and # tags out of the text. The editor has a per block handle menu, a slash menu, and @ and # popups. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: What decides the left sidebar?
a: The page does, through Shell's menu snippet. CampaignPage renders the map table of contents when tab is maps and MenuPanel otherwise; that was the first page to vary it. The right drawer is always social and chat. Settled 2026-09-08.

q: How do nested maps work?
a: Pin driven. A MapMarker carries link_map_id and CampaignMap now carries parent_map_id, set by linkMap in CampaignMaps when the DM points a pin at a child. Clicking the pin descends, and MapCanvas also fires onDescend when the zoom passes that pin's max_zoom, so zooming in walks down the tree. CampaignMaps draws a breadcrumb from the parent chain and CampaignPage builds the sidebar tree from tocRoots and childrenOf.

q: What do the page style rules in test/pages.spec.ts enforce?
a: Four things, and they fail the gate. No absolute length in a page style, so 6rem or a 20px shadow offset must become a token or calc over --space-n; every page variable must be built from a var() or be a bare percentage. No character outside ASCII in a page, so a text glyph standing in for an icon must be an Ornament. Every auto grid track needs minmax(min(...)) so it cannot overflow sideways. Learned by failing all four on CampaignPage 2026-09-08.

q: How is the campaign overview laid out?
a: A dynamic grid, no Panel boxes, settled 2026-09-08. The crown carries the name and a camp-stats tile row (Players, Heroes, Sessions, Quests, Maps, Pins). Under it camp-bar is position sticky with the tab shortcuts. Then camp-grid at 1fr plus a 24 percent rail: Characters as cards, an expandable Introduction, then Quests, Cast and The World as camp-plot groups down the main column, with a camp-feed of everything that happened in the rail. Mirrors MainPage's hall-plot and hall-divide idiom.

q: What happens at an unknown route?
a: The router resolves it to the Hearth on its own; the NotFoundPage fallback in App.svelte is never requested, confirmed by it never appearing in the dev server log. Only the address stayed wrong, so MainPage's onMount now does history.replaceState to /main whenever it renders at any other path. CharacterPage does the same by navigating to /main when getCharacter returns nothing or throws. NotFoundPage.svelte is dead code.

q: Does the AI character source import work?
a: Yes, with a Replicate key on the user document. Fed the D&D Beyond fighter and human markdown from reference/dndbeyond it read class Fighter and race Human correctly and the create flow carried them through. It does not set max hit points, so a level 5 fighter lands on the sheet at 0/1 HP. Measured 2026-09-08.

q: Where do local test fixtures live?
a: reference/seed/ with maps, portraits and audio subfolders and a SOURCES.tsv naming the licence and Commons page for each file. reference/ is gitignored so none of it reaches git. The class and race markdown under reference/dndbeyond/ is what the character source import is fed. Local test only, never shipped. The rows a local run starts with are a different thing: test/seed/, the api steps just seed runs.

q: Which campaign writers have no UI behind them?
a: postEncounter and deleteCharacter. Both exist on the services and both work when called, but nothing under src/components or src/pages calls either: the campaign has no Encounters tab and a character can only be removed by hand. Measured 2026-09-08 while seeding; the encounter and the character purge both had to go through the service module in the browser console.

q: What toggles the drawers?
a: Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + S, handled by stepDrawers on svelte:window in Shell. It cycles in turn through the drawers the page actually gave: none to menu to chat to none. The Sigil handles on the bar still toggle each one directly.

q: Is a thick accent coloured left border allowed?
a: No. The user ruled it out for anything 2026-09-08. .dnd-menu-row and .dnd-menu-note carried a border-inline-start of --border-width in --menu-line, --menu-line-strong on hover and --menu-accent on the active turn; all four are now a full hairline border that changes colour instead.

q: Why do the sheet breakpoints use container queries?
a: Because the sheet lives inside Shell, whose content box is narrower than the viewport whenever a drawer is open, so viewport media queries fire at the wrong time and the grid tracks overlap. Shell's .dnd-shell-hold carries 'container: page / inline-size' and CharacterPage uses @container page (max-width: 1200px) and (max-width: 760px). Any page inside Shell can key off the same 'page' container.

q: Were any Sigil frame traces broken?
a: Yes, two. cusped jumped to y=96 on the bottom-left and never closed symmetrically, which is why the dialog close button looked broken. lobed's relative curve chain ran off to x=109, outside the 0-100 viewBox. Both were rewritten as symmetric paths 2026-09-08: cusped as an eight point square star, lobed as an octofoil of eight radius 13 arcs about centre 50,50.

q: Where do the extra slots on the sheet come from?
a: From rules.resolved.derived, filtered by the bespokeSlots list in CharacterPage ('initiative','armorClass','speed','maxHitPoints') which the hardcoded slots already draw. dnd5e therefore contributes Carry Capacity, Spell Save DC and Spell Attack with no code. Same pattern as RulePanels skip, so a system that adds a derived value gets a slot for free.

q: How is the character sheet laid out?
a: Three bands then three columns, settled with the user 2026-09-08. Band one is sheet-band: the crown at 1fr and HitPoints at 22rem, stretched to the same height. Band two is sheet-slots: Proficiency, Walking, Inspiration, Initiative, Armor, then every rules derived value not in the bespokeSlots skip list, in an auto-fit 7rem grid. Band three is Abilities, the same auto-fit grid. Then sheet-grid at 0.85fr 1.15fr 2fr: the left column holds SavingThrows, Special, Senses, Proficiencies, RulePanels and DefensesNConditions; then Skills; then MainTabs.

q: How thick is the Sigil rim?
a: var(--border-width), 2px, with the inner key line at var(--border-hair) and the key scaled 0.88. It was a hardcoded stroke-width 5 which read as too heavy at sm size; the user asked for smaller, better borders 2026-09-08. Both strokes are vector-effect non-scaling-stroke so the width holds at every sigil size.

q: Does the Hearth shell header carry the new character and new campaign buttons?
a: No. The nav snippet on MainPage.svelte was removed 2026-09-08 at the user's request. The hero acts Forge a Character and Raise a Campaign, plus the section header Sigils, are the only entry points. Shell guards the nav rail with {#if nav} so nothing is left behind.

q: Why does task.sh board report zero for every status?
a: The board cache at .git/lcp/board.tsv is stale from an older column layout. Its stamp is the tasks dir mtime, the newest task mtime and the file count, so touching any task file rebuilds it. Learned 2026-09-08.

q: Where do the sheet's saves and skills come from?
a: From the declared rule system through $rules.resolved.saves and .skills, not the stored character arrays. A character with no stored savingThrows or skills still shows the six saves and eighteen skills dnd5e declares. Decided 2026-09-08.

q: What does task.sh serve stop leave behind on this repo?
a: The pnpm dev and vite children keep listening on 5173 after task.sh serve stop, because it kills only the recorded nohup pid; a following just dev then takes 5174 or 5175 while test/walk.sh is fixed on 5173. After serve stop, find the listener with lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 -sTCP:LISTEN and kill it before starting another server.

q: Does watch.sh <role> --wait survive as a background command in a role session?
a: No. The harness sends TERM to the background watch the moment the turn ends, every time: eight consecutive tester watches on 2026-09-07 died within seconds of arming with the board unmoved, and lcp_stop.sh then demands a new one, so a resting role session loops between the stop hook and the harness. A role session cannot rest on the watch; the user re-enters the role command when the board moves, and a resting session is best left with the loop interrupted.

q: What does the hearth carry, and what is not a thing on it?
a: A friends list along one side, campaigns laid horizontally on the left, characters as a grid, then a Lore section: one list with dividers gathering quests, chronicles, maps, characters, places and encounters. Party, cast and catalog are not things on the hearth. User, 2026-09-07.

q: What did the user find wrong with the hearth grid that 145 landed, on 2026-09-07?
a: An even grid of ten equal cells in a structure that does not follow how the app is built, header plates and rail heads on every panel that should not be there, broken cards, horizontal scroll back on the character and campaign rails, and content clipped so it cannot be read. Panels must differ in focus and size by what they are, and the layout must make sense with how the app is structured.

q: Is a party a thing outside a campaign?
a: No. A party exists only inside a campaign, so the hearth carries no party panel and nothing aggregates party members across campaigns. User, 2026-09-07.

q: How are two tasks whose scopes share a source file worked on the one primary checkout?
a: One after the other, or the second inside its own worktree. task.sh land commits every change under a task's scope paths, so a second task's uncommitted edit to a shared file is swept into the first task's commit and lands under the wrong id.

q: Why does the dev server answer 504 Outdated Optimize Dep after just gate, and what is the order of a walk and a gate?
a: just build, which just gate runs last, removes node_modules/.vite, so the dev server on 5173 loses its optimized deps and every module request answers 504 until it is restarted; a reload does not rebuild the cache. Run just walk before task.sh gate for a group, and after a gate bring the server back with task.sh serve stop then task.sh serve http://localhost:5173 just dev before the next walk.

q: How is test/walk.sh run?
a: just dev must serve localhost:5173 and the playwright session must already exist and be fresh: playwright-cli -s=walk close, then playwright-cli -s=walk open, before every walk. walk.sh checks the server with curl but never opens the browser, so every page fails with 'timed out waiting for ...' when the walk session is closed, and a session left signed in at the hearth from an earlier run dies on its first eval at /login with 'Execution context was destroyed' because the signed in shell navigates away. The walk's own trap closes the session at exit. A DOM check that follows a click waits with wait_for; the tracker's empty state renders a beat after the section opens.

q: Can a campaign carry an encounter through the app?
a: No. postEncounter at src/lib/firestore.service.ts:648 has no call site anywhere in src, so nothing in the UI ever writes a CampaignEncounter. The model, the rules and MainMenu's initiative tracker all exist since 104 and 105, but the write path is unreachable: every campaign shows the empty tracker until Firestore is seeded by hand. Found reviewing 145 on 2026-09-07.

q: What does the review state hold, and where does the body's Summary go?
a: Summary collapses into frontmatter and ## Review. All four roles stay. A task reaches review only when an agent flags it unsolvable by AI alone; /lcp-review spools through those, the AI helps as far as it can and writes what it cannot settle into .claude/questions for /lcp-questions.

q: Where does task ordering live, and what is the review state for?
a: Ordering is frontmatter alone: parent is the reverse of depends, relations are siblings, depends spans parents. ## Order is dropped and ## Done when is the only reconciliation target. review means a human is required, not a second machine pass. done is set only when synced to GitHub and closed by a PR.

q: How is a folder written in a task's Scope section?
a: Bare, no trailing slash and no glob: 'src/pages/main'. scope_of strips the '*' from '/**' leaving a trailing slash, and lcp_gate tests "$s"|"$s"/*, which becomes 'src/pages/main//*' and matches no file, so every write into the folder is denied.

q: How is the Replicate proxy path written?
a: Absolute, '/replicate'. Written relative it resolves against the current route, so on /campaign/:id it became /campaign/replicate/... , missed the vite proxy at vite.config.ts:27 and parsed index.html as JSON. ai.ts:37 and chat.ts:305, 3000, 3069 already carried the leading slash.

q: How is test/walk.sh run?
a: just dev must serve localhost:5173 and the playwright session must already exist: playwright-cli -s=walk open. walk.sh checks the server with curl but never opens the browser, so every page fails with 'timed out waiting for ...' when the walk session is closed.

q: How many worker sessions run on this repo at once?
a: One. The user confirmed on 2026-09-07 that the only worker is the session in front of them, so a task sitting in doing with an exited agent is stale, not held, and the worker session takes it back rather than waiting for another worker to finish it.

q: Does watch.sh <role> --wait hold as a background command in a reviewer session?
a: No. Five consecutive reviewer watches were killed before firing, each leaving .git/lcp/reviewer.pid clear, as already recorded for tester. lcp_stop.sh asks for the watch again on every stop, so the session loops arming one that never holds. The user re-enters the role command when the board moves.

q: Does watch.sh worker --wait hold as a background command in this session?
a: No. Five consecutive worker watches were killed before firing, so no wake reached the session. The same was already seen on the tester watch, so it is not role specific: a resting role session here cannot rely on the watch and the user re-enters the role command when the board moves.

q: Does watch.sh <role> --wait survive as a background command in a role session?
a: Not always. Three consecutive tester watches were killed before firing, each leaving .git/lcp/tester.pid clear, so no wake reached the session. When the background watch will not hold, the role session cannot rest on it and the user re-enters the role command when the board moves.

q: Does docs/inspiration carry a README?
a: No. It is images only, no README and no per entry source or licence index. Where a reference needs a source, the session searches the web for a similar sourced image rather than asking the user for an origin. User, 2026-09-07.

q: Why does the dev server answer 504 Outdated Optimize Dep after a build?
a: just build runs rm -rf node_modules/.vite, so a dev server already up on 5173 serves 504 for every prebundled dep until it is restarted. Measure a layout against just preview on 4173 instead, or restart just dev after a build.

q: Where do an encounter's turn actions and recommendations come from?
a: The rules engine, never Replicate. What it offers is controlled by settings on the encounter, which inherit their defaults from the campaign. This keeps engine.md intact: the actions stay declared under public/sources/systems and no branch in a component decides one. Decided by the user 2026-09-06.

q: How does a stale role watch pid from a /clear'd session clear itself?
a: watch.sh <role> --wait exits on its own when HEAD moves, so a pid left in .git/lcp/<role>.pid by a /clear'd session is released at the next commit on the branch. A new role session refused with '<role> is already waiting in this repo, pid N' re-arms after that commit and never kills the pid itself.

q: Who decides which combatants group together in an encounter?
a: Whoever holds access, on the campaign or on the resource itself. It is not a fixed friend or foe field decided by the DM alone. Stated by the user 2026-09-06 alongside the free position map.

q: How are things positioned on a map?
a: Free position, never a grid. Markers carry x and y and are placed anywhere, and encounter pieces are placed the same way. Zoom behaves like Google Maps: markers load and reposition as it changes and a different image is served near and far, which is the existing MapLayer min_zoom and max_zoom band. Places are clickable.

q: How are resources linked to each other across the app?
a: A tag system carrying the descriptors. Tags link lore, docs, objects, places and npcs together, and are what makes generating a character sheet, its images and a play loop recommendation possible. Nothing of it exists; CharacterMetadata.tags is the only tags field today and nothing reads it. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: What does sharing a character mean?
a: A link. The recipient opens a read only view of the sheet, rendered by a viewing mode of the character creator, and then chooses to copy it into their own. Share is the link, copy is the snapshot, and the viewer is a surface that does not exist yet. Decided by the user 2026-09-06.

q: What is an encounter meant to become?
a: A 2D battle map. Combatants, npcs and objects are pieces moved on a shared map, the encounter is marked on the map so a player sees where they stand, and proximity can be turned on. Combatants group into sides, a turn tracker runs, and each character's turn shows its available actions as clickable items with recommendations. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: What chat surfaces does the app owe?
a: Three. A campaign channel, a direct chat between two users, and temporary secret breakout chats between a subset of a campaign's members. Today only the campaign channel exists, at campaigns/{id}/chat gated on membership. Decided by the user 2026-09-06.

q: Does a campaign own its maps, npcs, locations and quests?
a: No longer. Every resource is created independently in its own folder, searchable on its own, and shared into a campaign by link with edit rights granted to users or campaigns. The campaign brings them together and the DM controls reveal. This replaces the four subcollections data.md describes. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: How is a player found and shown in the discover directory?
a: Searched by username or email, but email is never revealed until that user consents on their own screen. A row shows portrait and username only. The portrait loads only while the peer is online to seed it, so presence must exist outside a campaign; peers today sit under campaigns/{id}/peers. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: Who appears in the discover directory and how do two players connect?
a: Every signed in user, no opt out, searchable by the whole app. Decided by the user on 2026-09-06. Connection is a friend request: one player sends, the other accepts, and friendship is what the discover area is built on. firestore.rules line 22 already lets any signed in user read any profile.

q: Does the app have a discover area where players find each other?
a: No, and the user wants one: a global directory to inspect another player's pages, invite to chat and to a campaign, and share or copy a character or campaign. No invite exists anywhere, and firestore.rules line 73 lets only the DM write a campaign, so no player can self join without a rules change.

q: What is the reference for the campaign map?
a: Legend Keeper, named by the user on 2026-09-06, with additions on top. The existing model already matches it: zoom banded layers and markers, nested maps via link_map_id, and pins carrying record_kind and record_id rather than prose. MapCanvas.svelte does wheel zoom, pointer drag, layer pick by zoom and the is_visible reveal filter.

q: How does a tester wave run so the dev server and the gate are not rerun per task?
a: Agents write tests in parallel and execute nothing. The session runs the gate once for the whole wave through task.sh run, which holds one execution lock per checkout, and task.sh serve reuses the one dev server. task.sh land takes several ids and puts the wave in one commit, so a test that reached another task's code fails visibly.

q: Where does a failed task go, and where does the failing output live?
a: Failed is the worker's queue beside staged and task.sh next prints it first; the task keeps its base and a new agent field so the agent that wrote the code fixes it. Staged is the human handoff, never a failure lane. Failing output goes to test/<id>/ via task.sh result; Findings is one line per defect naming that file.

q: Is the first gothic design pass what the user wants the app to look like?
a: No. On 2026-09-06 the user called the panel frames broken, text size unhandled and off the theme, the top bar due for a complete redesign, and everything looking weird. Colouring, theming, texture, frames, design and completeness all need to be far better, starting from a second round of fantasy UI inspiration found online and written into docs/inspiration/README.md.

q: Does dndcs have an encounter or initiative data model?
a: Yes, since 104 and 105 landed. firestore.types.ts carries CampaignEncounter and EncounterCombatant, with CombatantKind covering 'npc'; campaignService exposes postEncountersListener. MainMenu.svelte renders the tracker from that model in initiative order, so the honest empty state now only shows when no campaign or no live encounter is present.

q: What happens to the worker watch when /clear is run in a resting worker terminal?
a: The watch.sh worker --wait process survives /clear under the same claude process and keeps .git/lcp/worker.pid, so a second --wait is refused with 'worker is already waiting in this repo'. Its wake no longer reaches the cleared conversation. The user kills the old pid or types /lcp-worker again when the board moves; the session may not kill it itself.

q: Should the tool buttons in the bar vary their sigil frames?
a: No. The user on 2026-09-06 called the mixed plate, star, cusped, lobed and ring frames in the sheet bar random and wants every bar tool the same design, drawn from docs/inspiration/8.png, the forged HUD with circular sigil buttons. Only the glyph inside differs between two bar tools; the frame is decided once, not per call site.

q: Does the user want any fixed pixel size in the dndcs UI?
a: No. The user wants every size dynamic: a token from src/app.css, a fraction of the container or a clamp, never a fixed pixel width or height. Stated during the 110 browser walk on 2026-09-06 and the reason 127 strips fixed sizes from the sheet; a hairline border is the one exception.

q: What did the user find wrong with the character sheet on 2026-09-06?
a: Overflow with no dynamic resizing, uneven oversized buttons off the inspiration layouts, panels grouped oddly with weak frames, portrait frames far simpler than the reference, and dialogs seen off centre. The sheet should take much more from docs/inspiration.

q: How should layout sizes be set across the app?
a: Nothing is fixed anywhere: every panel, board, dialog and button is sized dynamically from the viewport and its content, never a fixed pixel width or height. Stated by the user on 2026-09-06 after seeing the sheet board overlap the ability column with a drawer open.

q: Where does the reference text and art for class and race documents come from?
a: D&D Beyond, named by the user on 2026-09-06 as the reference the table uses for classes, races, their content and images. The fetched set lives under reference/dndbeyond/, gitignored and never shipped, pulled by scripts/reference.sh through just reference <kind>. Documents under public/sources stay hand authored and nothing is generated from the set.

q: Should 110 run solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired, or should it carry a headless driver a worker agent can run instead?
a: Neither the Chrome extension nor an agent. 110 runs solo in a worker session through the playwright MCP driving Brave for the visual walk, signed in as WALK_EMAIL from .env, and playwright-cli at /opt/homebrew/bin/playwright-cli is the scripted driver, boarded as 118 under test/. The Chrome extension is never used; the user rewrote 110 by hand in commit afa9aab on 2026-09-06.

q: Which browser and driver does browser verification use?
a: playwright with Brave, through the playwright MCP and playwright-cli. The Chrome extension and the claude-in-chrome tools are never used again.

q: Should the worker agent that 110 was dispatched to write the playwright-cli walk under test/ now, leaving the extension walk and the findings to the solo session that q-001 named, or should 110 stay untouched until the worker session takes it solo?
a: The agent writes nothing. Task 110 is taken solo by the worker session in the main conversation, which does both halves: the playwright-cli walk under test/ and the extension walk with the findings, because only the solo session holds the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools and one scope lands as one commit.

q: Should 110 run solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired, or should it carry a headless driver a worker agent can run instead?
a: Both. 110 runs solo in a worker session with the Chrome extension paired for the visual walk, and the same session runs playwright-cli, installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/playwright-cli, as the scripted driver. The user asked for both on 2026-09-06; the earlier answer of no headless driver is superseded.

q: Which elements are duplicated on the sheet in the second screenshot, taken after 113 and 115 landed? The image shows the six ability boxes, the six saving throw tiles, the skills table and the stat boxes once each, so the duplicate is not visible in the frame sent.?
a: Nothing is duplicated. The user was wrong: the sheet scaled out of the screen, so elements looked repeated. No sixth sub task under 112; the overflow is already boarded as 117.

q: Which sheet parts move into a dialog beyond 113, 114 and 115?
a: Only customization options: anything picked or configured on a thing, like the portrait frame picker, gets a dialog on that thing. Display blocks such as saving throws, Defences and Conditions, Grit, Senses and passive skills stay. The frame dialog needs more complex frame designs.

q: What supplies the twenty three pieces of catalogue art: SVG emblems authored in the repo's own Ornament idiom, or raster files you drop under public/ yourself?
a: Author the twenty three pieces as SVG emblems in the repo's own Ornament idiom, under public/sources/art/ and addressed as plain paths. The repo already draws its whole ornamental vocabulary as inline SVG in Ornament.svelte and Sigil.svelte, nothing in the app generates raster art, and an emblem set stays consistent with the gothic language the pages carry.

q: Should 110 run solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired, or should it carry a headless driver a worker agent can run instead?
a: Run 110 solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired. The walk needs a rendered page and a signed-in Firebase session, and the main conversation is the only context that holds the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools, so no headless driver is added and no new task is created.

q: How is a die roll recorded?
a: writeRollLog(type, text, formula, roll, total, details) in engine.ts. formula is passed at each of the ten call sites, never regexed from display text. RollLogItem adds author, set only on entries read back from the shared campaign log, so ChatItem renders it as a field.

q: Where does the shared campaign chat and roll log live?
a: campaigns/{id}/chat/{entryId}: author_id, author_name, kind (message|roll), body, query, is_hidden, roll_kind, formula, dice, roll, total, created_at. campaignService.postChatListener orders by created_at. getChatLog() in chat.ts scopes off currentRoute into currentCampaignId, mirrors local rollStore and replicateStore appends up, and falls to localStorage when no campaign is in scope.

q: Does dndcs have an encounter or initiative data model?
a: No. firestore.types.ts carries Campaign, CampaignSession, CampaignQuest, CampaignNpc, CampaignLocation, CampaignMap and MapMarker only; campaignService exposes no encounter call and COLLECTIONS names no encounter collection. The MainMenu Encounter tracker section renders an honest empty state until one is defined.

q: Why does a Button focus ring vanish in dndcs ui primitives?
a: clip-path on an element clips its own outer box-shadow, so var(--focus-ring) on a clipped root is invisible. The fix used in src/components/ui/Button.svelte, Slot.svelte and Stat.svelte: keep the interactive root unclipped (background: none) and hold the silhouette in a --*-shape custom property applied via clip-path to absolutely positioned frame/face/sheen layers. The root then carries box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) normally.

q: How are classes and races modelled?
a: Identically. src/lib/catalog.ts is the one loader for both kinds: getCatalog(kind), getCatalogEntry(kind, id), postCatalogReading(kind, sources) and getCatalogFacts(kind, entry). Documents are public/sources/classes/*.json and public/sources/races/*.json with an index.json per directory listing ids. There is no built-in versus custom distinction: an uploaded class is read into the same shape, cached by putCatalogEntry, and sits in the same list. src/components/CatalogList.svelte is the one vertical picker both steps use, carrying the define-your-own upload row and a link to /sources/:kind/:id. The create flow is character then class then race, and the race step is the one that writes the character.

q: Where does the ability list on the create page come from?
a: public/sources/systems/<id>.json attributes, loaded with getSystem. It is never a const in a component: gunslinger.json already declares a 7th attribute grt, and engine.md forbids hard coding a system. CharacterCreatePage renders one box per declared attribute, evaluates the declared modifier expression with getExpressionValue, and carries its own added attributes on creationData.attributes so the character can declare one nobody else has. getAbilities already takes Record<string, number> so an arbitrary id set needs no change downstream.

q: How does a file reach another player?
a: src/lib/swarm.ts, torrent style. The file: record carries blocks, an array of SHA-256 base64 hashes of the original split at 64KB, plus block_size. Presence sits at campaigns/{id}/peers/{uid}.{session} with a 20s beat and a 60s stale cutoff, signalling at campaigns/{id}/signals, deleted as read, lower peer id offers. Firestore carries presence only: availability is asked over the data channel with have?/have, blocks with want and a binary frame prefixed by a 4 byte request id. Each block is verified against its hash and a failing block is asked of the next holder. count 0 means no floor so the swarm is awaited, otherwise the floor renders at once and the original is pulled in the background into media/. No TURN, so a symmetric NAT pair falls back to the floor.

q: How does a player run dndcs?
a: Each player clones the repo and runs just dev. The dev server is part of the product: the /replicate proxy reaches the API without CORS, and the /media/ store in vite.config.ts reads and writes real files under media/ (gitignored) with ETag, If-None-Match and byte ranges. This replaced the frontend only and static rule in setup.md. A hosted dist still builds but has neither proxy nor media store, so AI and full size media need the local client.

q: Why was the profile empty on a page that mounts at load?
a: auth.init swapped getProfile for subscribeToProfile and stopped awaiting it, so isLoading went false before the first onSnapshot arrived. App.svelte renders the Router on !isLoading, so UserPage mounted with userProfile null and its onMount seeded displayName from nothing. Anything reactive still filled in later, which is why the email showed and the name did not. The subscription is now awaited for its first snapshot alongside getUserDetails before isLoading clears.

q: Why did uploads fail with Failed to process files?
a: public/pdf.worker.min.js was a July 2025 copy while pdfjs-dist is 6.3.289. pdf.js refuses a worker whose version does not match the API, so getDocument threw on every PDF. src/lib/sources.ts now resolves the worker from the installed package with import workerSrc from 'pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs?url', so it can never drift. The file in public/ is dead.

q: How are the menu and chat drawers opened?
a: From the Shell bar. MenuPanel and Chat each carried a position:absolute toggle at left:-50px / right:-50px, which the drawer aside clips with overflow:hidden, so neither drawer could be opened. Shell now holds menuOpen and chatOpen state, draws two Sigils in the bar, and sizes the grid columns from those. The --size-menu-curr and --size-chat-curr root variables are no longer written by anything.

q: What owns the page frame in dndcs?
a: src/components/ui/Shell.svelte. A 68px bar (crest or menu handle, back, title, nav snippet, profile chip, sign out, chat handle), optional menu and chat drawers driven by its own $state, a backdrop snippet layer, and a dnd-scroll content column held at narrow 860px, wide 1200px or full. Every authenticated page renders inside it. Page roots must never set their own 100vh or overflow-y: #app is absolute inset:0 overflow hidden, so a page that scrolls itself gets clipped.

q: Is Firebase the hosting target for dndcs?
a: No. The user ruled out Firebase for hosting dndcs, so hosting proposals must not assume Firebase Hosting, Firestore-backed realtime or Cloud Functions as the host. Where it will be hosted instead is not settled by this.

q: How are files stored and shared in dndcs?
a: Each player's files live in a personal folder by default, using the same file system and employee approach as nimployer. Sharing is an opt-in step afterwards: the owner chooses to share a file or folder with others, so nothing is shared on upload.

q: How are a player's uploaded files owned and shared in dndcs?
a: Each player's files sit in a personal folder, following the same files approach as nimployer's employees. A file belongs to its owner by default, and the owner chooses whether to share it, as with resources in the Access dialog.

q: How does a player start Quillborne locally?
a: They tell their agent "start local dev", which follows .claude/skills/start-local-dev/SKILL.md; the README only points there. A local run needs no shared secret: SAUTH_DEBUG_USER_ID signs in as the debug user and skips Samna Auth, the nimling modules are public, and SAUTH_DEBUG_PRIVATE_SEED is each machine's own 64 hex characters from openssl rand -hex 32. Settled with the user 2026-11-06.

q: How does a local run get its test data, and why not SQL?
a: just dev runs just seed after the migrations: test/seed/ holds JSON steps, each an api call as a debug player (testy or pip), run in process through handler.PutRoutes with a middleware that sets user_id per step, the way test/go calls handlers. Over HTTP the debug middleware signs every request in as Testy, so Pip could not act; SQL would have to make claims, which data.md forbids outside the handlers. A feature a player sees updates its steps in the same branch (CLAUDE.md rule 17). Settled with the user 2026-11-06.

q: How do several worktrees run local dev at once?
a: Each checkout has a slot n: service 4290+n, Postgres 5490+n, Azurite 10000+n, Vite 5173+n (strictPort). The ports live in that checkout's own .env (SERVER_PORT, PGPORT, the BlobEndpoint port) because the service overloads env from .env; containers, volume and db image are named after the checkout folder. start-local-dev step 2 picks the lowest free slot from 1 for a worktree; the main checkout is slot 0. Settled with the user 2026-11-06.

q: Where do vehicles live in Quillborne?
a: Vehicles came over from the stand-alone vehicle platform on 2026-11-06. A vessel is a vehicle row behind /api/vehicle, read on /main/vehicles/:id with the stops Deck, Design, Crew, History, Rules and Papers; the Dock is /main/vehicles and a campaign's fleet /main/campaign/:id/vehicles, reached from the World section of the campaign bar, the Vehicles fold of the navigator and Visit the Dock on the hearth. The platform's workspace is the campaign, its GM the DM, its profiles the signed in players and its personas the characters.

q: How are vehicle rules kept as data?
a: A vehicle system is a JSON document under web/public/sources/systems/vehicles/ listed in its index.json. The catalogue, layouts, templates, perks, open rules questions, thresholds, penalties and condition texts are data, and every rule a ruling switches names its ruling in the document, so no ruling id or component key is written in code. web/src/lib/rules/vehicle.ts is the interpreter. A vessel's overlay adds homebrew components by key for that vessel alone.

q: Whose stats does a vehicle use?
a: The character the reader sails as. The deck's Aboard as picks one of the reader's sheets, preferring one on the crew, then one seated in the vessel's campaign, then one with crew standing in that system, then the last played. Its abilities and proficiency come from the rules engine through getCrewResolved, and its crew level and perks are character.crew[<vehicle system id>], so the perks follow the character from ship to ship.

q: Who may change a vehicle?
a: A steward, the builder or the campaign DM, changes anything. The Crew claim, read and write, goes to the players whose characters are on the crew; they change states and requests, and components and stats only while customisation is approved or full. Approved components are checked on the web against playerAvailable, since the service holds no rules. A crewman who may not save a design asks the DM with a request, which the steward approves or declines in Design. A components change carries the revision it was drafted on and answers 409 when stale.

q: Does every new feature in Quillborne need a CLI with a built MCP server, reachable from both the API and the CLI?
a: Yes. Every feature is exposed through the API and through a CLI, and the CLI carries a built MCP server for it. This is added in the same work as the feature, not later and not for one side only.

q: What is the command line tool for Quillborne called?
a: qubo. The user named it.

q: Does Quillborne need a GitHub token such as GH_REPO_TOKEN for the build, migrate or local run, and where does the Replicate key live?
a: No. samna-auth-middleware and the other repos are not public and need no GH_REPO_TOKEN, so no GitHub token is kept in .env, locally or on tst. The Replicate key is personal: it is never in .env, not even on tst. It is a per-player key stored as a Samna Auth secret, set and removed on /user, and the service alone opens it.

q: In Quillborne, should the web's API types be generated or hand-written?
a: Generated, never hand-written. Generate them with tygo from internal/db, the way bookable and nimployer do, so the types follow the Go models and nothing is written by hand.
